analysis: Both changed files are Swift test files only: MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineTests.swift (new tests at head lines 336-414 for JSON response-format thinking defaults for Qwen templates) and InboundDecodeTests.swift (new reasoningBudgetExtracted test at head lines 288-310). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache storage, or encryption paths are modified, so none of the threat-model assets or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041) are directly affected. The tests document behavior implemented elsewhere: template context control of enable_thinking for JSON response formats, and extraction of a positive reasoning.max_tokens budget from the sealed body (including float forms and rejection of non-positive, overflow, and non-numeric values). Test-only behavior can't introduce a runtime regression. The tests do hint at production changes in unseen files (ProviderLoop.extractChatTemplateControls, reasoningBudgetTokens, resolvingPromptDate, templateAdditionalContext) that were not supplied here. Those should be reviewed in their own batch for input-handling concerns: the budget parsing must stay bounded, and sealed-body fields must stay consumer-controlled only in the prompt rendering path. Observed test code contains no secrets or network behavior. No findings from these units.
